title: kv-cache: adaptive memory manager and eviction prioritization for fragmentation/paging/spillover
author: Asha Mehta
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and aggressive spillover to host memory have been a root cause of intermittent OOMs and elevated p99 latency on long-context workloads. This PR implements an adaptive memory manager and eviction prioritization that reduces fragmentation, defers unnecessary paging, and schedules background compaction to improve tail latency and reduce OOMs. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a segment-based allocator that tracks free segment runs to reduce internal fragmentation; 2) Add adaptive eviction priorities that consider sequence reuse probability (LRU + decay + reuse-score) and token cost; 3) Implement opportunistic coalescing and background compaction runs with a bounded CPU budget and backoff policy; 4) Improve spillover paging: instead of immediate device->host spill on every eviction, we now apply an eviction staging policy (hot/cold classification) and only page cold segments proactively while keeping warm segments in a short-term spill buffer; 5) Add instrumentation and guards: metrics for fragmentation ratio, average segment run length, spill rate, page-in latency, and an OOM early-warning gauge; 6) Add config flags and safe rollout: feature-flagged, canary rollout, and dynamic thresholds tuned by workload. Design notes: - Allocation: segment-based allocation replaces target-size-first fit with a best-fit-with-coalescing heuristic. We keep a small free-list cache for tiny allocations to avoid churn. - Eviction scoring: score = w1 * recency_decay + w2 * reuse_score + w3 * token_cost + w4 * fragmentation_penalty. We tuned weights based on offline traces (see commits). - Background compaction: compaction is throttled by a token-bucket so it does not interfere with inference throughput; compaction priority is lowered on high GPU utilization. - Paging: cold segments are aggregated and paged as larger contiguous host chunks to reduce page fragmentation and kernel overhead. Hot segments fall into a short-lived spill buffer in pinned host memory to accelerate page-in when reused. Testing and results: unit + integration tests added; e2e perf bench on A100-80GB and V100-32GB clusters with long-context tests (seq_len 16k) show: 1) 32% reduction in observed fragmentation ratio; 2) 18% reduction in p99 token latency under sustained load; 3) 78% reduction in device OOM rate in our stress harness; 4) overall CPU overhead for compaction ~3-5% with throttling. Rollout plan: feature flag enabled in dev followed by canary on 5% of production capacity for 48h; metrics monitored include fragmentation_ratio, spill_rate, page_in_latency, inference_p99, and device_oom_count. If regressions >5% on inference_p99 or any increase in device_oom_count, automatic rollback. Checklist: - [x] allocator and eviction prototype - [x] unit tests for allocator/coalescer - [x] integration tests for staging/paging - [x] perf harness runs - [x] metrics and dashboards - [x] canary rollout plan

discussion:
Diego Alvarez (reviewer): Can you clarify how reuse_score is computed from prefix overlap traces?
Asha: reuse_score is computed from a sliding-window estimate of observed prefix reuse in training traces (exponential moving average); details in eviction_policy.cc comments.
Priya Nair: The compactor might compete with inference on CPU-heavy nodes, can we gate by GPU utilization?
Asha: Yes, compaction token-bucket pauses when GPU utilization > 85% or when inference latency SLOs are breached; added tests and metrics.
Samir Patel: Suggest adding a canary kill-switch in the config - resolved, added infra/deploy/canary-config.yaml.
Diego: Approved after addressing fragmentation metrics and adding dashboards.
Final: 3 approvals and one post-merge cleanup noted.
